name: Fuzzy dark matter as a cosmic matter wave
summary: Ultralight bosonic dark matter obeys the Schrodinger-Poisson system, a Gross-Pitaevskii equation with self-gravity; galaxy halos develop solitonic cores and granular interference like condensates.
breaks: Interaction is long-range self-gravity rather than contact scattering; occupation is classical and not reached by thermal condensation; no trap or superfluid flow measurement.

name: Fermi pressure from trapped atoms to white dwarfs
summary: Degeneracy pressure measured in trapped Fermi gases is the same Pauli effect that supports white dwarfs and neutron stars against gravity.

name: Cold molecular collisions and astrochemistry
summary: Interstellar chemistry at 10-100 K proceeds by barrierless ion-molecule reactions and tunnelling, the same low-temperature collision physics that cold-molecule experiments resolve state by state.

name: Quasars choose settings in cosmic Bell tests
summary: Cosmic Bell tests used the colours of photons from high-redshift quasars (emitted about 7.8 and 12.2 Gyr ago) to pick measurement settings. Any freedom-of-choice conspiracy would then have to have been set up before that light was emitted.

name: Density-matrix kinetics of relic neutrinos
summary: Neutrino decoupling with flavour oscillations is computed with Sigl–Raffelt density-matrix quantum kinetic equations. These combine a commutator term with collision terms that damp flavour coherence, much as dephasing does, but are nonlinear and not of Lindblad form. The result is N_eff ≈ 3.044, used in CMB fits.

name: Zero-point energy and the cosmological-constant problem
summary: Summing field-mode zero-point energies to a high cutoff predicts a vacuum energy far above the observed dark-energy density; the Casimir effect does not settle the issue because it measures energy differences.
breaks: Casimir forces arise from charge fluctuations and do not measure absolute vacuum energy; renormalization makes the naive cutoff estimate unphysical.

name: Superconducting photon sensors for sub-GeV dark matter
summary: Superconducting single-photon detectors (SNSPDs, TESs) have sub-eV energy thresholds. They have been proposed and used as targets and sensors for keV–MeV dark matter scattering off electrons, and for absorption of sub-eV dark photons and ALPs.

name: Antihydrogen: trap plasmas meet precision spectroscopy
summary: Antihydrogen is made by merging antiproton and positron plasmas in Penning–Malmberg traps, using rotating-wall compression and evaporative and sympathetic cooling. It is then probed by 1S–2S and hyperfine spectroscopy and compared with hydrogen to test CPT symmetry.

name: Nonlinear Schrödinger: BEC solitons and Langmuir collapse
summary: The Gross–Pitaevskii equation and the envelope equation for Langmuir waves (Zakharov, with the ponderomotive density cavity) are both cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equations. Both show dark and bright solitons, modulational instability and collapse above a critical norm: the attractive-BEC 'bosenova' corresponds to Langmuir collapse and to laser self-focusing.
breaks: In a plasma, ψ is a classical wave envelope and the nonlinearity comes from the slow ion-acoustic density response, which is instantaneous only in the subsonic limit. In a BEC, ψ is the macroscopic wavefunction with contact interactions.

name: Ultracold neutral plasmas from laser-cooled atoms
summary: Photoionizing laser-cooled atoms just above threshold makes neutral plasmas with electron temperatures of a few kelvin and sub-kelvin ions, reaching Γ>1. Disorder-induced heating caps ion coupling near Γ≈2–3; laser-cooling the plasma ions themselves pushes it higher.

name: Bohm potential in quantum hydrodynamics of dense plasma
summary: The Madelung (1926) hydrodynamic rewriting of the Schrödinger equation, whose quantum potential de Broglie–Bohm theory also uses, supplies the 'Bohm term' in quantum hydrodynamic models of dense and warm dense plasmas. Its prefactor and validity beyond the long-wavelength limit are disputed.

name: High-frequency Floquet expansion gives ponderomotive force
summary: For a fast, spatially varying drive, the high-frequency (Kapitza/van Vleck) effective Hamiltonian of Floquet theory reproduces the ponderomotive potential of laser–plasma theory. The term enters at order 1/ω² because the first-order commutator vanishes. Both expansions fail near resonances, where driven heating sets in.

name: Paul-trap pseudopotential = ponderomotive potential
summary: In the nonrelativistic, adiabatic limit (small Mathieu q; quiver amplitude much smaller than the field-gradient scale), the time-averaged force holding an ion in an RF Paul trap (Dehmelt pseudopotential) is the ponderomotive force that expels electrons from an intense laser focus. Ion micromotion is the electron's quiver motion. Relativistic laser intensities (a₀ ≳ 1) lie outside this shared regime.
breaks: For a_0\gtrsim1 the laser case becomes relativistic (cycle-averaged \gamma), which never happens in ion traps. A Paul trap also needs Mathieu stability (q\lesssim0.9), a condition with no counterpart in a laser focus.

name: Adiabatic invariant μ ↔ conserved quantum number
summary: The magnetic moment μ that makes mirror traps work is the gyration action, an adiabatic invariant. Ehrenfest's 1916 adiabatic hypothesis made such invariants the quantities to quantize; this led to the quantum adiabatic theorem. Semiclassically μ = (n+½)|q|ħ/m, with n the conserved Landau-level index.
breaks: In fusion plasmas n\sim10^7 for 10 keV electrons at 5 T, so only the classical invariant matters there. Classical μ is conserved only asymptotically (exponentially small breaking), while the quantum theorem needs a spectral gap.

name: Gamow tunnelling sets the fusion reactivity
summary: Fusion at 10–20 keV works only because nuclei tunnel through the Coulomb barrier. The barrier-penetration factor times the Maxwellian tail gives the Gamow peak. That peak fixes ⟨σv⟩, the best D–T temperature and the Lawson triple product.

name: Chern numbers of magnetized plasma waves; edge modes
summary: Band-topology ideas built on Berry curvature have been applied to the cold magnetized-plasma dielectric. Its wave bands carry nonzero Chern numbers, and bulk–edge correspondence predicts one-way, backscatter-immune edge waves at plasma boundaries. Experimental confirmation is still pending.

name: Wigner–Moyal equation reduces to Vlasov as ħ→0
summary: The Wigner transform of the mean-field (Hartree) von Neumann equation gives the Wigner–Poisson equation. It reduces to Vlasov as ħ→0, with O(ħ²) corrections. Quantum plasma kinetics, quantum Landau damping and the quantum Lenard–Balescu operator are built on this formalism.

name: Ramsauer–Townsend minimum shapes argon discharges
summary: Ar, Kr and Xe are nearly transparent to electrons of ~0.2–0.7 eV because the s-wave phase shift passes through π. This minimum in the momentum-transfer cross section distorts electron energy distributions, mobility and breakdown in discharges. Partial-wave cross sections are fed into the Boltzmann solvers used for plasma processing.

name: Photon in plasma: effective mass ħω_p; plasmons
summary: Transverse waves in a plasma obey ω²=ω_p²+c²k², a massive Klein–Gordon dispersion. So photons in a plasma act as quasiparticles of mass ħω_p/c², which lets them decay into neutrino pairs in stars. Quantized longitudinal Langmuir oscillations are plasmons.
breaks: The mass is a medium effect tied to the plasma rest frame, and longitudinal and transverse modes differ. No vacuum gauge symmetry is broken; this is the analogy behind the Anderson–Higgs mechanism, not an identity with it.

name: Spin and positronium physics in PET
summary: Para-positronium (C=+1) annihilates to two back-to-back 511 keV photons by charge-conjugation and momentum conservation, fixing the PET signature; ortho-Ps (3γ) is mostly quenched in tissue.

name: Squeezing and entanglement-enhanced sensing
summary: Squeezed and entangled probe states beat the standard quantum limit toward the Heisenberg limit, applied in interferometers, magnetometers and spin ensembles.

name: Black-hole shadows and S2 orbit as strong-field tests
summary: The EHT ring diameters of M87* and Sgr A* agree to about 10% with the Kerr shadow size, which barely depends on spin, a strong-field test of the metric. GRAVITY and Keck measured S2's combined gravitational redshift and transverse Doppler shift (2018–19), and GRAVITY measured its Schwarzschild periastron precession (2020).
breaks: The ring is emission from plasma, not the shadow edge itself. Its calibration relies on GRMHD models and on mass priors, which limits how far the test can reach.

name: Energy conditions, area theorem and generalized 2nd law
summary: Through the Raychaudhuri equation and the Einstein equations, the null energy condition makes horizon area non-decreasing (Hawking's area theorem, the 'second law'). Hawking radiation carries a negative energy flux across the horizon, so it violates the NEC and the area can shrink. Bekenstein's generalized second law then replaces the area theorem.

name: AdS black holes as thermal CFT states (Hawking–Page)
summary: In AdS/CFT a large AdS–Schwarzschild black hole is dual to the boundary CFT at temperature T_H, with entropy A/4G equal to the CFT's thermal entropy. The Hawking–Page transition between thermal AdS and the black hole maps to the confinement/deconfinement transition of the gauge theory, and quasinormal decay maps to thermalization.
map: T_H=T_{\rm CFT},\ S_{BH}=\frac{A}{4G}=S_{\rm CFT};\ \ T_{\rm HP}=\frac{3}{2\pi\ell}\ (\text{AdS}_5,\ \hbar=c=k_B=1)\leftrightarrow T_{\rm deconf}
breaks: Small AdS black holes have negative heat capacity and are unstable, like asymptotically flat ones. The duality is cleanest at large N and strong coupling.

name: Horizon area quanta and black-hole entropy in LQG
summary: LQG's discrete area spectrum lets one count the spin-network punctures of an isolated horizon. The count gives S ∝ A, equal to A/4 only for one Barbero–Immirzi value (γ ≈ 0.24–0.27, by scheme). The SU(2) treatment gives a −(3/2) ln A correction; other schemes give different coefficients.
breaks: Matching A/4 requires fixing γ by hand, and Hawking radiation itself has not been derived from the LQG dynamics.

name: D-brane microstate counting reproduces A/4G
summary: Strominger and Vafa counted BPS bound states of D-branes with the charges of a 5D extremal black hole. At leading order in large charges, the degeneracy reproduces A/4Għ, the first exact microscopic match. Near-extremal extensions reproduce Hawking emission with the correct greybody factors.
breaks: The count is controlled only for supersymmetric or near-extremal black holes. Schwarzschild-like black holes far from extremality are not covered.

name: Islands and the Page curve from holographic entropy
summary: The Ryu–Takayanagi formula, extended to quantum extremal surfaces, computes the entropy of black-hole radiation. For an evaporating black hole coupled to a bath, a new extremal surface (an island) appears after the Page time, and the entropy then follows the unitary Page curve. AdS/CFT also gives the main argument that evaporation is unitary, because the dual CFT evolves unitarily.
breaks: The derivations are cleanest in AdS or in low-dimensional JT-gravity models. How information gets out in a local, operational sense, and the status of the result in asymptotically flat spacetime, are still debated.

name: Semiclassical origin of the paradox and of islands
summary: Hawking's 1976 argument comes from QFT in curved spacetime: late radiation is entangled with partner modes behind the horizon, so its fine-grained entropy rises monotonically, eventually exceeding S_BH. The island formula keeps generalized entropy A/4Għ + S_bulk but extremizes over gravitational saddles (replica wormholes), recovering the Page curve.
map: |\Psi\rangle\propto\sum_n e^{-\pi n\omega/\kappa}|n\rangle_{\rm out}|n\rangle_{\rm in}\Rightarrow S_{\rm rad}\uparrow;\ \ S_{\rm gen}=\frac{A}{4G\hbar}+S_{\rm bulk}

name: EMRIs map the Kerr multipole structure
summary: A compact object spiralling into a massive black hole completes ~10⁴–10⁵ orbits in LISA's band. Ryan's theorem says that, for stationary axisymmetric vacuum spacetimes, the phase evolution encodes the mass and current multipoles. Checking Kerr's relation M_ℓ+iS_ℓ=M(ia)^ℓ tests the no-hair theorem with projected precision far beyond electromagnetic probes.
breaks: Extracting the multipoles needs second-order self-force waveforms and handling of environmental effects such as accretion disks. Both are still under development.

name: Linearized Einstein equations give gravitational waves
summary: Writing g = η + h and choosing harmonic (Lorenz) gauge turns the Einstein equations into a sourced wave equation. In transverse-traceless gauge two polarizations travel at c. Far from a slow source the leading retarded solution is the quadrupole formula, and its Isaacson energy flux drives binary inspirals.
map: \Box\bar h_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{16\pi G}{c^4}T_{\mu\nu},\ \ h^{TT}_{ij}=\frac{2G}{c^4r}\ddot I^{TT}_{ij},\ \ P=\frac{G}{5c^5}\langle\dddot Q_{ij}\dddot Q_{ij}\rangle

name: Einstein equation as an equation of state
summary: Jacobson (1995) derived the Einstein equations by requiring the Clausius relation δQ = T dS on every local Rindler horizon. He used the Unruh temperature, an entropy proportional to area and the Raychaudhuri equation; Λ appears only as an integration constant. The result motivates emergent and entropic-gravity proposals in which the field equations are thermodynamic rather than fundamental.
breaks: The derivation assumes local equilibrium and an area law. With higher-curvature entropy or out-of-equilibrium horizons it needs extra terms, and whether gravity is truly emergent remains contested.

name: Extra polarizations and dipole radiation beyond GR
summary: GR predicts two tensor polarizations and emission that starts at quadrupole order. Scalar–tensor theories add a breathing mode and dipole radiation from binaries with unequal sensitivities, entering at −1PN. Massive gravity adds dispersion and five polarizations, and generic metric theories allow up to six. Waveform models capture these effects as PN-coefficient deviations or ppE terms.

name: GW170817 speed of gravity prunes Horndeski theories
summary: In Horndeski theories, couplings of the scalar to curvature (the G_{4,X}, G_{5,X} and G_{5,φ} terms) make tensor waves travel at a speed different from c on a cosmological background. GW170817 and GRB 170817A arrived 1.7 s apart after ~40 Mpc, bounding the gravity–light speed difference at the 10⁻¹⁵ level. This eliminated most such dark-energy models and also bounds Lorentz violation in the gravity sector.
breaks: The bound applies at LIGO frequencies (~100 Hz). Theories whose c_T deviates only at much lower frequencies, near the cutoff scale of the dark-energy effective theory, are not excluded by it.

name: Curvature-squared terms from quantum fields: R² gravity
summary: Renormalizing quantum matter fields on a curved background requires R² and R_{μν}R^{μν} counterterms in the gravitational action. Starobinsky's 1980 inflation model began as a quantum correction driven by the trace anomaly. Its R² term is now the prototype f(R) theory, which is equivalent to GR plus a scalar field (the scalaron).
map: f(R)=R+\frac{R^2}{6M^2}\ \Leftrightarrow\ \text{GR}+\text{scalaron of mass }M;\ \ \mathcal L_{\rm ct}\supset a_1R^2+a_2R_{\mu\nu}R^{\mu\nu}

name: Binary-pulsar orbital decay confirms quadrupole formula
summary: The orbital period of the binary pulsar PSR B1913+16 decays as the Peters–Mathews quadrupole energy loss predicts, to about 0.2%. This was the first, indirect evidence that gravitational waves carry energy. The double pulsar J0737−3039 now tests the same formula to about 10⁻⁴.

name: Strong-field tests of GR with compact-binary signals
summary: The PPN approach of fitting parametrized deviations from GR carried over to gravitational-wave data. LVK analyses test GR through shifts in the post-Newtonian phase coefficients, inspiral–merger–ringdown consistency, ringdown spectroscopy, and a graviton-mass bound from dispersion (m_g ≲ 1.3×10⁻²³ eV/c²). These probe the dynamical strong-field regime that solar-system and pulsar tests cannot reach.
breaks: Unlike the PPN framework, there is no complete theory-agnostic parametrization of the strong field. Waveform systematics can mimic deviations.

name: Planck-scale discreteness vs Lorentz-invariance bounds
summary: Some discrete or emergent spacetime models (for example early LQG semiclassical states and lattice-like discreteness) predict Planck-suppressed modified photon dispersion. Fermi GRB timing pushes the linear-order scale past E_Pl, disfavouring such models. Causal sets evade the bound because Poisson sprinkling is statistically Lorentz invariant, and deformed rather than broken symmetry is another way out.
breaks: Quadratic-order effects (∝E⁴/E_Pl²) remain far below current sensitivity. Not every approach predicts dispersion: asymptotic safety and CDT make no generic Lorentz-violating prediction.

name: Rindler horizons and the Unruh effect
summary: A uniformly accelerated observer follows an orbit of a Lorentz boost (hyperbolic motion) and sees a Rindler horizon. Restricted to the Rindler wedge, the Minkowski vacuum is thermal with respect to the boost generator (Bisognano–Wichmann), which gives the Unruh temperature. Near any non-extremal horizon the geometry is approximately Rindler, so this flat-spacetime effect is the core of Hawking radiation.
map: x^2-c^2t^2=\frac{c^4}{a^2};\ \rho_{\rm R}\propto e^{-2\pi K_{\rm boost}},\ k_BT_U=\frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c}\leftrightarrow k_BT_H=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi c}
breaks: The Unruh temperature for laboratory accelerations is tiny (~4×10⁻²¹ K per m s⁻²), so it has not been observed directly.

name: Primordial black holes as dark matter
summary: PBHs are a non-particle dark-matter candidate; Hawking evaporation removes those below about 5e14 g and gamma-ray and CMB limits constrain slightly heavier ones, while lensing and GW limits leave the asteroid-mass window open.
map: t_{\rm evap}\approx\frac{5120\pi G^2M^3}{\hbar c^4}\ (\text{photons only})\Rightarrow M\approx2\times10^{14}\,\text{g};\ \text{all SM species}: M\approx5\times10^{14}\,\text{g}

name: The cosmological constant problem
summary: Lorentz invariance forces vacuum energy to enter the Einstein equations as ρ_vac g_μν, so QFT zero-point energy, the Higgs potential and the QCD condensate all contribute to Λ. Naive estimates exceed the observed (2.2 meV)⁴ by roughly 40 (QCD) to 120 (Planck cutoff) orders of magnitude.
map: \langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\rm vac}=-\rho_{\rm vac}g_{\mu\nu}\Rightarrow\Lambda_{\rm eff}=\Lambda+8\pi G\rho_{\rm vac}/c^4,\ \rho_{\rm obs}\approx(2.2\,\text{meV})^4
